docs.title: Project LLM Management
docs.text:
Welcome to the GitHub-based Project Management with LLM Agents template!

This is a comprehensive, production-ready template for managing software projects using:

  • 🏗️ GitHub Projects v2 for centralized tracking
  • 🤖 LLM Agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) for automation
  • 🔄 GitHub Actions for CI/CD and workflows
  • 👥 Human oversight via a central Project Board

docs.title: Automated Workflows
docs.text:
• Branch Creator: Automatically creates feature branches when issues receive the auto-branch label
  • Code Reviewer: AI-powered code reviews on pull requests
  • Test Feedback: Automated testing, linting, and coverage reporting

docs.title: Project Management
docs.text:
• Backlog View: All future work, sorted by priority
  • Priority Board: Kanban-style tracking by status
  • Team Items: Personalized view filtered by owner

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
• Seamless GitHub Projects v2 integration
  • Multiple LLM provider support (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini)
  • Full CI/CD pipeline with automatic status updates

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git
  • GitHub account with admin access
  • GitHub CLI (gh)
  • Python 3.11+ (if using Python workflows)

docs.title: 2. Clone/Fork this template
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-org/project-llm-management.git
cd project-llm-management

docs.title: 3. Configure GitHub Secrets
docs.text: Go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and add: - CLAUDE_API_KEY (for code review) - GH_TOKEN (GitHub token with repo access)

docs.title: 4. Enable GitHub Projects v2
docs.text:
• Navigate to your repository's Projects tab
  • Click New project and select Table or Board
  • Workflows will sync project updates automatically

docs.title: 5. Create your first issue
docs.text:
• Use one of the provided templates (Feature, Bug, Task)
  • Add the auto-branch label
  • A branch will be created automatically!

docs.text: Pour adapter le template à vos besoins spécifiques.

docs.title: Changer le naming des branches
docs.text:
Éditer .github/workflows/create-branch.yml :

# De : feat/{number}-{title}
BRANCH_NAME="feat/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"

# À : feature/{number}-{title}
BRANCH_NAME="feature/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"

# Ou : naming basé sur le type
if [[ "$LABELS" == *"type:bug"* ]]; then
  BRANCH_NAME="fix/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"
else
  BRANCH_NAME="feat/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"
fi

docs.title: Ajouter des champs custom au Project Board
docs.text:
1. Créer le champ manuellement sur GitHub ou modifier scripts/setup_project_fields.py :
fields_to_create = {
    "Status": [...],
    "Sprint": ["Sprint 1", "Sprint 2", "Sprint 3"],  # Nouveau champ
}
  1. Mapper dans update-project.yml :
- name: Update sprint field
  run: |
    if [[ "$LABEL" == "sprint:1" ]]; then
      python scripts/project_sync.py --issue $NUM --sprint "Sprint 1"
    fi

docs.title: Notifications Slack/Discord
docs.text:
Ajouter à n'importe quel workflow :

- name: Notify Slack
  run: |
    curl -X POST ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }} \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"text":"✅ PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} merged!"}'

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration
docs.text: Comment personnaliser le template selon vos besoins.

docs.title: .github/project.yml
docs.text:
project:
  number: 1  # 👈 Changez selon votre projet
  name: "Project Backlog"
  auto_link: true

fields:
  status:
    options: ["Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done"]
    default: "Backlog"
  priority:
    options: ["Low", "Medium", "High"]
    default: "Medium"

À modifier : - project.number : Mettez le numéro de votre projet GitHub

docs.title: Labels GitHub
docs.text:
Les labels sont créés par setup-project.sh. Pour les personnaliser :

# Modifier setup-project.sh ligne 86+
declare -a LABELS=(
    "type:feature:0e8a16:New feature"
    "priority:urgent:ff0000:Urgent"  # Ajoutez vos labels
)

docs.title: 🚀 Guide de démarrage

# Installer Git si nécessaire:
# macOS: brew install git
# Linux: sudo apt install git
# Windows: https://git-scm.com/download/win

docs.title: 2. GitHub CLI
docs.text:
# Installer GitHub CLI
# macOS
brew install gh

# Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)
curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo dd of=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg
sudo apt install gh

winget install GitHub.cli

gh --version

docs.title: Option A : Utiliser comme template (recommandé)
docs.text:
1. Sur GitHub, cliquez sur le bouton "Use this template" en haut de la page
  2. Donnez un nom à votre projet (ex: mon-projet)
  3. Choisissez visibilité (Public ou Private)
  4. Cliquez "Create repository from template"

docs.title: Étape 2 : Authentification GitHub (30 secondes)
docs.text:
# Connectez-vous à GitHub
gh auth login

# Suivez les instructions :
# 1. Choisissez "GitHub.com"
# 2. Choisissez "HTTPS"
# 3. Dites "Yes" pour authentifier
# 4. Choisissez "Login with a web browser"
# 5. Copiez le code et ouvrez le navigateur

docs.title: Créer un GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT)
docs.text:
1. Allez sur : https://github.com/settings/tokens/new
  2. Donnez un nom : Mon template automation
  3. Cochez ces scopes :
  4. ✅ repo (Full control of private repositories)
  5. ✅ project (Full control of projects)
  6. ✅ workflow (Update GitHub Action workflows)
  7. Cliquez "Generate token"
  8. Copiez le token (vous ne le reverrez plus !)

docs.title: Configurer le token
docs.text:
# Configurez le token GitHub
gh secret set GH_TOKEN
# Collez votre token quand demandé

# (Optionnel) Configurez la clé API Claude pour la revue de code IA
gh secret set CLAUDE_API_KEY
# Obtenez votre clé sur : https://console.anthropic.com/

💡 Note : Sans CLAUDE_API_KEY, la revue de code fonctionnera en mode basique (sans IA).

docs.title: Étape 4 : Installation (2 minutes)
docs.text:
# Installez les dépendances Python
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Lancez le script de setup
./setup-project.sh

Le script va : 1. ✅ Vérifier que tout est installé 2. ✅ Créer les labels GitHub (type:feature, priority:high, etc.) 3. ✅ Créer un GitHub Project v2 4. ✅ Vous demander de noter le numéro du projet

🔔 Important : Notez le numéro du projet affiché (ex: Project #1)

docs.title: 5a. Mettre à jour le numéro de projet
docs.text:
Éditez le fichier .github/project.yml :

project:
  number: 1  # 👈 Remplacez par le numéro de votre projet
  name: "Project Backlog"

docs.title: 5b. Auto-créer les champs custom
docs.text:
# Créez automatiquement les champs du Project Board
python3 scripts/setup_project_fields.py --project-number 1 --owner VOTRE_NOM

Cela crée automatiquement : - Status : Backlog, Ready, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done - Priority : Low, Medium, High - Effort : 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 (story points) - Type : Feature, Bug, Task, Docs, Infrastructure - Target Version : (champ texte libre)

Si vous voyez ✅ All checks passed!, c'est prêt ! 🎉

docs.text: Documentation de tous les scripts d'automation du template.

docs.title: 1. setup-project.sh
docs.text:
Rôle : Script de setup initial pour configurer un nouveau projet

Utilisation : 

./setup-project.sh

Ce qu'il fait : 1. ✅ Vérifie les prérequis (gh, python, jq) 2. ✅ Détecte le repository GitHub courant 3. ✅ Crée tous les labels nécessaires 4. ✅ Crée un GitHub Project v2 5. ✅ Configure le workflow de base

Labels créés : - Type : type:feature, type:bug, type:task, type:docs, type:infrastructure - Priority : priority:high, priority:medium, priority:low - Status : status:backlog, status:ready, status:in-progress, status:blocked, status:done - Special : auto-branch, good-first-issue, help-wanted

Arguments : Aucun (interactif)

Prérequis : - GitHub CLI authentifié - Permissions d'admin sur le repository

Sortie : 

🚀 GitHub Project LLM Management - Setup Script
================================================

✅ Prerequisites check passed
Repository: username/project-name
✅ Labels configured
✅ Project created: #1

docs.title: 2. scripts/setup_project_fields.py
docs.text:
Rôle : Crée automatiquement les champs custom du Project Board via GraphQL

Utilisation : 

python3 scripts/setup_project_fields.py \
  --project-number 1 \
  --owner YOUR_USERNAME

Arguments : - --project-number : Numéro du projet (visible dans l'URL) - --owner : Propriétaire du projet (username ou organisation) - --project-id : (Optionnel) ID GraphQL du projet (alternative à --project-number)

Ce qu'il fait : 1. ✅ Cherche le projet par numéro 2. ✅ Vérifie les champs existants 3. ✅ Crée les champs manquants : - Status (Single Select) : Backlog, Ready, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done - Priority (Single Select) : Low, Medium, High - Effort (Single Select) : 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 - Type (Single Select) : Feature, Bug, Task, Docs, Infrastructure - Target Version (Text)

Variables d'environnement : - GH_TOKEN ou GITHUB_TOKEN : Token GitHub avec scope project

Sortie : 

🔍 Checking existing fields...
📋 Creating custom fields...
  ✅ Created field: Status
  ✅ Created field: Priority
  ⏭️  Field 'Effort' already exists, skipping...
✅ All fields configured!

Gestion d'erreur : - Si le projet n'existe pas → Erreur explicite - Si le champ existe déjà → Skip (pas de doublon) - Si le token n'a pas le bon scope → Erreur explicite

docs.title: 3. scripts/validate_setup.sh
docs.text:
Rôle : Valide que le template est correctement configuré

Utilisation : 

./scripts/validate_setup.sh

Ce qu'il vérifie : 1. ✅ Prérequis : gh, python3, git installés 2. ✅ Repository : Dans un repo git avec remote GitHub 3. ✅ Authentification : GitHub CLI authentifié 4. ✅ Secrets : GH_TOKEN et CLAUDE_API_KEY configurés 5. ✅ Labels : Tous les labels requis existent 6. ✅ Project : Au moins un projet existe 7. ✅ Workflows : Tous les workflows sont présents 8. ✅ Dépendances : Packages Python installés

Sortie (succès) : 

🔍 GitHub Project Template - Setup Validation
==============================================

[1/8] Checking prerequisites...
  ✅ GitHub CLI (gh) installed
  ✅ Python 3 installed (3.11.5)
  ✅ Git installed

[2/8] Checking repository context...
  ✅ Inside a Git repository
  ✅ Repository: username/project-name

...

==============================================
✅ All checks passed! Template is ready to use.

Please fix the errors above before using this template.

Codes de sortie : - 0 : Tout OK - 1 : Erreurs trouvées

docs.title: 4. scripts/project_sync.py
docs.text:
Rôle : Synchronise les issues/PRs avec le Project Board via GraphQL

Utilisation : 

# Synchroniser une issue
python3 scripts/project_sync.py \
  --issue 123 \
  --status "In Progress" \
  --priority "High"

# Synchroniser une PR
python3 scripts/project_sync.py \
  --pr 456 \
  --status "In Review"

# Spécifier un projet
python3 scripts/project_sync.py \
  --issue 123 \
  --project 1 \
  --status "Done"

Arguments : - --issue NUMBER : Numéro de l'issue à synchroniser - --pr NUMBER : Numéro de la PR à synchroniser - --project NUMBER : (Optionnel) Numéro du projet - --status VALUE : Définir le champ Status - --priority VALUE : Définir le champ Priority - --effort VALUE : Définir le champ Effort - --type VALUE : Définir le champ Type - --version VALUE : Définir le champ Target Version

Variables d'environnement : - GH_TOKEN ou GITHUB_TOKEN : Token GitHub - GH_OWNER : Propriétaire du repository - GH_REPO : Nom du repository

Comment ça marche : 1. Récupère l'ID GraphQL de l'issue/PR 2. Trouve le project (ou utilise le premier trouvé) 3. Ajoute l'item au project (si pas déjà ajouté) 4. Met à jour les champs demandés

Sortie : 

✅ Issue #123 synced successfully

Utilisé par : - Workflow update-project.yml (automatiquement) - Peut être appelé manuellement pour debug

docs.title: 1. .github/workflows/update-project.yml
docs.text:
Rôle : Synchronise automatiquement le Project Board avec les issues/PRs

Déclencheurs : - Issue créée → Ajoute au Backlog - Issue labellée → Met à jour Status/Priority/Type selon le label - PR ouverte → Met à jour Status à "In Review" - PR mergée → Met à jour Status à "Done"

Exemple de mapping labels : 

Label "auto-branch"       → Status: "Ready"
Label "status:in-progress" → Status: "In Progress"
Label "priority:high"      → Priority: "High"
Label "type:feature"       → Type: "Feature"

Variables d'environnement définies : 

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  GH_OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
  GH_REPO: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}

docs.text:
Rôle : Crée automatiquement une branche quand le label auto-branch est ajouté

Déclencheur : - Issue labellée avec auto-branch

Ce qu'il fait : 1. Récupère le titre de l'issue 2. Crée un slug (ex: "Fix bug API" → "fix-bug-api") 3. Crée une branche feat/{issue-number}-{slug} 4. Poste un commentaire avec les instructions git

Exemple : 

Issue #42 : "Add dark mode"
→ Branche créée : feat/42-add-dark-mode

Commentaire posté :
✅ Branch created: feat/42-add-dark-mode

Get started:
git fetch origin
git checkout feat/42-add-dark-mode

docs.title: 3. .github/workflows/code-review-agent.yml
docs.text:
Rôle : Analyse automatiquement les PRs avec Claude AI

Déclencheur : - PR ouverte, mise à jour, ou réouverte

Ce qu'il fait : 1. Récupère le diff de la PR 2. Envoie à l'API Claude avec un prompt structuré 3. Génère une revue de code avec : - ✅ Points forts - ⚠️ Suggestions d'amélioration - 🔴 Problèmes critiques 4. Poste la revue en commentaire

Mode fallback : Si CLAUDE_API_KEY n'est pas configuré, fonctionne en mode basique (checklist manuelle).

Modèle utilisé : claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022

docs.title: 4. .github/workflows/ci-tests.yml
docs.text:
Rôle : Exécute les tests et validations sur chaque PR

Déclencheur : - Push sur main/develop/staging - PR ouverte

Étapes : 1. ✅ Vérifier permissions des scripts 2. ✅ Valider la syntaxe YAML des workflows 3. ✅ Tester le setup script 4. ✅ Lancer les tests unitaires (pytest) 5. ✅ Vérifier la couverture de code

Matrice de tests : - Python 3.11

docs.title: Q: Do I need to pay for the API keys?
docs.text:
A: - Claude API: Anthropic uses a pay-as-you-go model. Free credits available for new accounts. - OpenAI: Also pay-as-you-go, but usually more expensive than Claude for code review. - Gemini: Free tier available, pay-as-you-go otherwise.

We recommend Claude for best code review quality and reasonable pricing.

docs.title: Q: Can I use this without LLM APIs?
docs.text: A: Yes! The template will still work: - ✅ Branch Creator: Works without API keys - ✅ CI Tests: Works without API keys - ⚠️ Code Review: Falls back to basic lint if no API key is set - ✅ Project Updates: Works without API keys

docs.title: Q: What Python versions are supported?
docs.text:
A: 3.11+ is the default. You can modify .github/workflows/ci-tests.yml to test against: 

python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]

docs.title: Q: Why isn't my branch being created?
docs.text: A: Check these: 1. ✅ Did you add the auto-branch label? 2. ✅ Is the Actions tab showing the workflow running? 3. ✅ Check workflow logs for errors: Actions → create-branch.yml → Latest run

docs.title: Q: Can I use a different branch naming convention?
docs.text:
A: Yes! Edit .github/workflows/create-branch.yml and modify the BRANCH_NAME variable:

# Current: feat/{number}-{slug}
BRANCH_NAME="feat/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"

# Custom example: bugfix/{number}-{slug}
BRANCH_NAME="bugfix/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"

docs.title: Q: Why did the Code Review Agent not comment?
docs.text:
A: Reasons: 1. CLAUDE_API_KEY not set in secrets 2. API rate limit exceeded 3. PR diff too large (limit: 10000 lines) 4. Workflow failed (check Actions logs)

Solution: Add the secret and test on a new PR.

docs.title: Q: Can I disable certain workflows?
docs.text:
A: Yes! Workflows have conditions. For example, to disable code review: 1. Go to .github/workflows/code-review-agent.yml 2. Add a condition in the jobs: section: 

jobs:
  code-review:
    if: false  # Disable this workflow

Or rename the file to .disabled to skip it.

docs.title: Q: How do I bulk update statuses?
docs.text:
A: Currently, GitHub Projects v2 doesn't have bulk edit via UI. You can: 1. Use GraphQL API for bulk updates 2. Use GitHub CLI: 

gh issue list --label "ready" | xargs -I {} gh issue edit {} --project "Project Board"

docs.title: Q: Can I automate status transitions?
docs.text:
A: Partially. Workflows can update statuses via GraphQL, but full automation requires: 1. Custom scripts in your repo 2. External tools (Zapier, Make, etc.) 3. Custom GitHub App

We recommend keeping human review for major status changes.

docs.title: Q: Why aren't my issues appearing in the project?
docs.text:
A: Issues auto-appear if: 1. ✅ Project is linked to the repository 2. ✅ Issue has the right filters (if any)

To manually link an issue: 1. Open the issue 2. Go to Projects section on the right 3. Click Add to project → Select your project

docs.title: Q: Why are my tests timing out?
docs.text:
A: GitHub Actions has limits: - Free tier: 6 hours per month per user (deprecated, now all public) - Jobs: 6 hours max per job - Workflows: 35-day retention

Solutions: 1. Optimize test suite (reduce expensive tests) 2. Use caching for dependencies 3. Run tests in parallel

docs.title: Q: Can I trigger workflows manually?
docs.text:
A: Yes! Add workflow_dispatch to any workflow:

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # Allows manual trigger

Then go to Actions → Workflow name → Run workflow

docs.title: Q: How do I see workflow logs?
docs.text: A: 1. Go to Actions tab 2. Click the workflow run 3. Click the failed job 4. Expand steps to see logs 5. Look for error messages

docs.title: Q: Can I run workflows locally?
docs.text:
A: Yes! Use act:

# Install
brew install act

# Run a workflow locally
act push

# Run specific job
act -j build

docs.title: Q: Will the AI leak my code?
docs.text:
A: No: - Claude: Anthropic doesn't use API calls for training (per their policy) - Code review only analyzes the diff, not full codebase - All processing is server-side and secure

However, always review third-party APIs' privacy policies.

docs.title: Q: Can I customize the code review prompt?
docs.text:
A: Yes! In .github/workflows/code-review-agent.yml, find this section:

prompt = f"""Review this GitHub Pull Request code changes...

Modify it to add your custom instructions: 

prompt = f"""Review this GitHub PR for our project.
Focus on: {your_priorities}
Ignore: {your_exclusions}
...

docs.title: Q: What's the typical cost per code review?
docs.text:
A: Claude (Anthropic): - ~$0.01 - $0.05 per review (depending on code size) - Much cheaper than OpenAI for this use case

Monitor spending: 

# Check Anthropic usage
gh api user

docs.title: Q: Can I use multiple LLM providers?
docs.text:
A: Not yet. The current implementation uses one provider. To support multiple: 1. Modify the code review script to choose provider 2. Use a config file or environment variable 3. Test each provider

Feature request: Consider opening an issue for multi-provider support!

docs.title: Q: How do I revert a merged PR?
docs.text:

# Option 2: Revert via GitHub UI
Go to PR → Click "Revert" button (appears after merge)

docs.title: Q: Can I rename a branch?
docs.text:
A: 

# Rename locally
git branch -m old-name new-name

# Rename remote
git push origin new-name
git push origin --delete old-name

Then delete the old branch on GitHub.

docs.title: Q: Why is my commit not linked to an issue?
docs.text:
A: Use the correct format in your commit message: 

git commit -m "feat: Add feature

Closes #123"  # Must say "Closes #123"

Or in PR description: 

Fixes #123
Resolves #456
Closes #789

docs.title: Q: I broke something. How do I reset?
docs.text:
A: 

# Undo last commit (keep changes)
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Undo last commit (discard changes)
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Undo to specific commit
git reset --hard {commit-hash}

⚠️ Be careful with --hard!

docs.title: Q: My workflow is in an infinite loop!
docs.text:
A: 1. Go to Actions tab 2. Click the stuck workflow 3. Click Cancel workflow (top right) 4. Fix the issue in the workflow file 5. Commit and push

Example infinite loop cause: 

# ❌ This causes infinite loop
on:
  push:
    paths: [".github/workflows/"]

jobs:
  update-workflow:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: git push  # Triggers workflow again!

docs.title: Q: How do I debug a failing workflow?
docs.text: A: 1. Check Actions → Failed workflow → Logs 2. Look for red text or error messages 3. Common issues: - Missing secrets: Could not resolve secret - Missing dependencies: ModuleNotFoundError - Wrong branch: Check on: [branches] - Permission issues: Check permissions: section

docs.title: Q: Can I get email notifications?
docs.text: A: Yes: 1. Go to Settings → Notifications 2. Enable GitHub Actions notifications 3. Choose: Always, Failing only, or Never

docs.title: Q: How do I customize the project fields?
docs.text: A: In your GitHub Project v2 settings: 1. Click Settings (gear icon) 2. Click Custom fields 3. Add/Remove/Rename fields 4. Update workflows to sync with new field names

docs.title: Q: Can I use this for non-Python projects?
docs.text:
A: Yes! Modify the workflows: - JavaScript: Change setup-python to setup-node - Go: Use setup-go - Rust: Use dtolnay/rust-toolchain

Update the CI commands accordingly.

docs.title: Q: How do I integrate with external tools (Slack, Discord, Jira)?
docs.text:
A: Options: 1. Webhooks: Send POST requests from workflows 2. GitHub Apps: Develop custom integrations 3. Zapier/Make: Connect without code 4. GitHub API: Custom scripts

Example: Slack notification 

- name: Notify Slack
  uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
  with:
    webhook-url: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Automatically creates a feature branch when auto-branch label is added to an issue.

docs.title: Trigger
docs.text:
on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
• Label name == auto-branch
  • Repository has write permissions

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
Issue labeled with "auto-branch"
         ↓
Extract issue #123 and title
         ↓
Slugify title: "Add auth" → "add-auth"
         ↓
Create branch: feat/123-add-auth
         ↓
Push to origin
         ↓
Comment on issue with instructions

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Branch created on origin
  • Comment posted with checkout instructions
  • No changes to main branch

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Issue: #42 "Implement payment system"
↓
Branch created: feat/42-implement-payment-system
↓
Comment:
✅ Branch auto-created: `feat/42-implement-payment-system`

Next steps:
1. git checkout feat/42-implement-payment-system
2. Make your changes
3. Push and create a Pull Request

BRANCH_NAME="feat/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${SLUGIFIED}"

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Run comprehensive code quality checks: formatting, linting, type checking, and tests.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop, staging]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

docs.title: Matrix Testing
docs.text:
matrix:
  python-version: ["3.11"]

Extend to test multiple Python versions: 

matrix:
  python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]

docs.title: 1. Checkout Code
docs.text: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

docs.title: 2. Setup Python
docs.text:
- uses: actions/setup-python@v4
  with:
    python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

docs.title: 3. Cache Dependencies
docs.text:
- uses: actions/cache@v3
  with:
    path: ~/.cache/pip
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('**/requirements*.txt') }}

docs.title: 4. Format Check (Black)
docs.text:
black --check --line-length 100 src/ tests/
- Verifies code formatting - Non-blocking (continue-on-error) - Suggests fixes if fails

docs.title: 5. Lint (Pylint)
docs.text:
pylint src/ --disable=C0111,W0212 --fail-under=7.0
- Checks code quality - Minimum score: 7.0/10 - Non-blocking

docs.title: 6. Type Check (Mypy)
docs.text:
mypy src/ --ignore-missing-imports
- Static type validation - Catches type errors early - Non-blocking

docs.title: 7. Run Tests
docs.text:
pytest tests/ \
  --cov=src/ \
  --cov-report=xml \
  --cov-report=html \
  --junitxml=test-results.xml
- Executes all unit tests - Generates coverage reports - XML output for CI integration

docs.title: 8. Report Results
docs.text:
# Comment on PR with results
gh issue comment {PR} --body "..."

Example comment: 

## ✅ Tests Passed

- Tests: 127/127 passed ✅
- Coverage: 85%
- Lint: OK (score: 8.5)
- Build: ✅

---
*Generated by GitHub Actions*

docs.title: Build Job (Optional)
docs.text:
If applicable, builds package distribution: 

python -m build

docs.text:
• ❌ Tests fail → Status: FAILURE
  • ⚠️ Lint warns → Status: SUCCESS (non-blocking)
  • 🔴 Type errors → Status: SUCCESS (non-blocking)

Note: Only tests are blocking by default.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Use Claude AI to automatically review pull requests and provide constructive feedback.

docs.title: Trigger
docs.text:
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• CLAUDE_API_KEY secret configured
  • PR should be < 10000 lines (limit)
  • Python with anthropic library installed

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
PR opened/updated
     ↓
Get PR diff (via gh cli)
     ↓
Prepare prompt with diff + PR description
     ↓
Call Claude API with prompt
     ↓
Parse response (structured markdown)
     ↓
Post as PR comment
     ↓
Update project status → "In QA"

docs.title: Prompt Structure
docs.text:
Review this GitHub PR code changes. Provide constructive feedback:

**PR Title**: {title}
**PR Description**: {description}

**Code Changes**:
```diff
{diff}

Provide review with: 1. ✅ Strengths 2. ⚠️ Suggestions 3. 🔴 Critical Issues 

### Claude Configuration
```python
client = Anthropic()
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
)

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
## 🤖 Automated Code Review by Claude AI

### ✅ Strengths
- Good separation of concerns
- Proper error handling
- Clear variable names
- Well-structured functions

### ⚠️ Suggestions
- Consider adding docstrings to public functions
- Use f-strings instead of .format()
- Extract magic number 100 to named constant
- Add more test cases for edge cases

### 🔴 Critical Issues
- **Security**: Line 45 - SQL injection risk, use parameterized queries
- **Performance**: Lines 30-35 - N+1 query problem in loop

---
*This is an informational review - approval is not required for merge*

docs.title: Change Model
docs.text:
model="claude-3-sonnet-20240229",  # Other Claude versions
# or
model="gpt-4",  # OpenAI fallback

docs.title: Increase/Decrease Detail
docs.text:
max_tokens=2048,  # More detailed review
max_tokens=512,   # Brief review

docs.title: Custom Instructions
docs.text:
Modify the prompt to focus on specific areas: 

prompt = f"""Review focusing on:
1. Security vulnerabilities
2. Performance optimizations
3. Code style consistency

{original_prompt}
"""

If CLAUDE_API_KEY not set:

Exemple de Feature Request :

Title: Add dark mode toggle

Description:
Users want a dark mode option for accessibility and reduced eye strain.

Motivation:
- Improve accessibility for users with light sensitivity
- Reduce eye strain during night usage
- Follow modern app standards

Acceptance Criteria:

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
# Clone this template
git clone https://github.com/your-org/project-llm-management.git
cd project-llm-management

git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/project-llm-management.git

docs.text:

# Python dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Development tools (for local testing)
pip install pytest black pylint mypy mkdocs mkdocs-material

docs.title: Step 3: Configure GitHub Secrets
docs.text:
Navigate to your repository settings:

Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions

Add the following secrets:

docs.title: GITHUB_TOKEN
docs.text:
GitHub automatically provides this, but you can also create a Personal Access Token:

gh auth login
# Select: GitHub.com
# Select: HTTPS
# Authenticate with browser

docs.title: CLAUDE_API_KEY (for Code Review)
docs.text:
1. Get your API key from console.anthropic.com
  2. Add it to your repo secrets:
gh secret set CLAUDE_API_KEY --body "sk-ant-..."

docs.title: OPENAI_API_KEY (Alternative to Claude)
docs.text: gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY --body "sk-..."

docs.title: GEMINI_API_KEY (Alternative to Claude)
docs.text: gh secret set GEMINI_API_KEY --body "AIza..."

docs.title: Step 4: Enable GitHub Projects v2
docs.text:
1. Go to your repository
  2. Click the Projects tab
  3. Click New project
  4. Select Table or Board view
  5. Name it: Project Board
  6. Create the project

docs.title: Custom Fields to Create
docs.text:
In the project settings, add these fields:

Field Name Type Values Priority Single select Low, Medium, High Effort Single select 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 Status Single select Backlog, In Progress, In QA, Done Owner People Auto (from assignee) Sprint Text v1.0, v2.0, etc. Environment Single select dev, preprod, prod

docs.title: 1. Backlog (Table)
docs.text:
• Columns: Title, Priority, Effort, Owner, Status
  • Filter: Status != "Done"
  • Sort: Created date (oldest first)

docs.title: 2. Priority Board (Kanban)
docs.text:
• Group by: Status
  • Filter: Priority = High OR Medium
  • Sort: Priority (highest first)

docs.title: 3. Team Items (Table)
docs.text:
• Columns: Title, Owner, Sprint, Status, Due Date
  • Filter: Owner = me (for personal view)

docs.title: Step 6: Configure Workflows
docs.text:
Most workflows are pre-configured, but verify they're enabled:

Settings → Actions → General

Ensure: - ✅ Actions workflows are enabled - ✅ Read/write permissions for Actions

docs.title: Create a test issue
docs.text:
gh issue create \
  --title "Test: Setup verification" \
  --body "Testing the workflow setup" \
  --label "auto-branch"

This should automatically: 1. Create a branch: feat/1-test-setup-verification 2. Post a comment with checkout instructions 3. Trigger the CI workflow

docs.title: Verify workflows ran
docs.text:
gh run list --workflow ci-tests.yml
gh run list --workflow create-branch.yml

docs.title: Step 8: Configure MkDocs (Documentation)
docs.text:
# Install MkDocs
pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material

# Build docs locally
mkdocs build

# Serve locally
mkdocs serve
# Visit http://localhost:8000

docs.title: Deploy to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
The workflow .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml automatically deploys when you push to docs/:

  1. Go to Settings → Pages
  2. Set source to Deploy from a branch
  3. Select gh-pages branch
  4. Save

Your docs will be available at: https://your-username.github.io/project-llm-management

docs.text:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

docs.text:
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
